# Net zero targets: China — Climate Action Tracker (June 2026 Update)

CAT evaluates China's net zero target as: **Poor** (comprehensiveness).

China submitted its Mid-Century Long-Term Low Greenhouse Gas Emission Development Strategy (LTS) on October 28, 2021 to the UNFCCC, which contains the country's commitment to reach "carbon neutrality before 2060". The commitment was first declared at the UN General Assembly in September 2020 by President Xi Jinping (Xinhua News Agency, 2020).

China's new Environmental Code, passed in March 2026, represents the country's first comprehensive climate legislation and provides a legal foundation for long-term decarbonisation toward its 2060 carbon neutrality goal (Xinhua News Agency, 2026b).

## Key elements
- Target year: 2060 ("carbon neutrality" before 2060).
- Emissions coverage: appears to apply only to CO2 emissions rather than all GHGs. However, researchers at Tsinghua University and China's Special Envoy for Climate Change, Xie Zhenhua, have stated that China's net zero target covers all GHG emissions (China Dialogue, 2021). In the absence of explicit confirmation in official policy documents, the CAT takes a conservative approach and assumes the LTS covers only CO2 until further official clarification.
- Legal status: net zero target in law (included in China's Environmental Code, passed March 2026, the country's first comprehensive climate legislation; also in the "1+N" carbon peaking/neutrality framework and the 15th Five-Year Plan).
- Reductions/removals outside own territory: relies on international offset credits or reserves right to use them.
- No separate reduction & removal targets; China only targets 80% share of non-fossil energy in 2060 (implying a large role for carbon removal). Tsinghua (2022) pathways show forest sinks of -7 to -8 GtCO2e/year and removals (CCS, BECCS) from -5 to -9 GtCO2e/year.

## Intermediate / sectoral targets (from LTS)
- China has pledged to reach peak carbon emissions by 2030 in its NDC, reiterated in the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) and the Action Plan For Carbon Dioxide Peaking Before 2030.
- Implement green building standards in 100% of new buildings by 2025.
- Achieve around 40% market share of vehicles sold for NEVs.
- Achieve a 25% forest coverage rate.
- Peaking and gradually reducing coal consumption during the 15th FYP period; reach a peak-plateau in oil consumption during the 15th FYP period.
